chunks: I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام—and Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā, from Ibn Isḥāq, from ʿAmr ibn ʿUthmān, from Ibrāhīm ibn ʿAbdillāh ibn Sām, said:
I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: A man has outstanding supererogatory prayers to make up, so many that he does not know how much they are due to their abundance. What should he do?
He said: “Then let him pray until, due to the abundance, he no longer knows how much he has prayed; then he will have made up an amount corresponding to what he owes.”

I said: Suppose he neglected it and cannot make it up because of his occupation. He said: “If his occupation is in seeking a livelihood that is indispensable, or attending to a need of a believing brother, then there is nothing upon him. But if his occupation is for worldly matters and he busied himself with them away from prayer, then making it up is upon him; otherwise he will meet Allah as one who treated lightly, was negligent, and wasted the sunnah (prophetic tradition) of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله.”
I said: If he is not able to make it up, is it proper that he give charity? He remained silent for a while, then said: “Yes, let him give charity.”
I said: And what should he give in charity? He said: “According to his means, and the minimum of that is one mudd.” Then he said: “One mudd to each poor person in place of each prayer.”
I said: And how much prayer is it for which one mudd is due for each poor person? He said: “For every two rakʿahs of the night prayer, and every two rakʿahs of the daytime prayer.”
So I said: He is not able. He said: “One mudd for every four rakʿahs.”
So I said: He is not able. He said: “One mudd for the night prayer, and one mudd for the daytime prayer. And prayer is better, and prayer is better, and prayer is better.”

key_terms.أَخٍ مُؤْمِنٍ: a fellow believing brother whose need may justify one’s occupation
key_terms.الْقَضَاءِ: making up missed acts of worship
key_terms.سُنَّةِ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ: the prophetic tradition of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله
key_terms.صَدَقَةٍ: charity given as a substitute when unable to perform the make-up
key_terms.مُدٌّ: a measured quantity of food given in charity

ai.seo_question: What should someone do if they owe many missed nawāfil prayers and cannot make them up?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the ruling regarding missed supererogatory prayers and how a person should make them up when their number is unknown. If one cannot perform the qaḍāʾ due to inability, charity may serve as a substitute according to one’s means, though actually performing the prayer remains superior. The report also distinguishes between being prevented by necessary livelihood or helping a believer, and being distracted by worldly pursuits.
